CHIEF DEEP RE-VERIFICATION of the four "documented promise" types, replacing the earlier shallow assessment. GENERAL CRITERION, which should be applied before ranking any future type: a forgeable type's documented promise survives the forge ONLY IF some field's type is BOTH unforgeable AND not otherwise obtainable. Both halves are required - a field type that is unforgeable but freely obtainable protects nothing, because a caller simply obtains one.

RESULTS - three of four promises fail, not four.

COVERAGE (features/estimate.scala:102): fields are two plain Ints, no payload dependency. fromProduct((0,5)) gives eligible=0, observed=5, so observed exceeds eligible and fraction is unbounded. FULLY BROKEN. This is the support carrier eight modules rely on.

CREDENCE (core/ids.scala:142): fields (Double, Option[Probability], Option[String]). Probability is an opaque type over Double with a legitimate public factory, so a valid instance is trivially obtainable. Forging (0.5, Some(p), None) yields a calibrated value with no named calibration model. FULLY BROKEN - and that promise is design-contract rule 3.

CHECKEDSIDECARPRELUDE (codec/sidecar.scala:329): fields (BlockedSidecarLayout, Vector[Checksum]). BlockedSidecarLayout is itself a private-constructor case class and therefore forgeable; Checksum is opaque over String with a public factory and therefore obtainable. Both payloads yield. FULLY BROKEN, on the type whose entire purpose is to witness a verification.

AUTHORIZEDREMOTEREQUEST (embed-core/privacy.scala:772): the raw-text promise SURVIVES. Its payload is PseudonymizedText, a plain final class - no Mirror, no fromProduct - obtainable only from the certifying pseudonymization path. It satisfies both halves of the criterion and is the POSITIVE EXAMPLE in this codebase of how a promise is made to hold. Its policy envelope still fails; see the earlier correction note.

SLICE AUTHORS: PseudonymizedText is the pattern to copy when a type must carry a guarantee - make the sensitive field's TYPE unforgeable and unobtainable, not merely the outer constructor private.
